terms.gdp_qoq: Real GDP: everything the US produces, after inflation. This is the change from the quarter before, scaled to a full year (annualized). About 2% a year is the long-run trend.
terms.gdp_yoy: Real GDP against the same quarter a year earlier: the smoother view of growth, without the quarter-to-quarter noise.
terms.unrate: Share of people looking for work who have none (BLS, monthly). The Fed's main jobs gauge: a rise of 0.5 pts in a few months has come before most recessions.
terms.claims: New claims for unemployment benefits in the week (Department of Labor). The earliest sign of layoffs; the 4-week average smooths out holidays and storms.
terms.cont_claims: People still claiming benefits. When it climbs, those who lost a job are taking longer to find a new one.
terms.cpi: Consumer Price Index: the prices households pay for a basket of goods and services (BLS). The inflation figure in the headlines.
terms.core_cpi: CPI without food and energy, which jump around. Shows the underlying trend of inflation.
terms.ppi: Producer Price Index, final demand: the prices businesses get for what they sell. Often moves ahead of consumer prices.
terms.core_ppi: PPI without food and energy: the steadier view of pipeline price pressure.
terms.pce: Personal Consumption Expenditures prices (BEA): wider than CPI, and the measure the Fed's 2% target is set on.
terms.core_pce: PCE without food and energy: the Fed's favourite inflation gauge. Near 2% means the job is done.
terms.fed: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between banks. Raising it cools the economy and inflation; cutting it supports growth and jobs.
terms.effr: The rate banks actually paid each other overnight; it sits inside the Fed's range.
terms.cycle: What the Fed has done over the last year: hiking (fighting inflation), cutting (supporting jobs) or on hold.
terms.expect: What fed funds futures prices imply for the next Fed decisions: the chance of a hold, a cut or a hike, the same reading CME FedWatch gives.
terms.CPI: Consumer prices against a year earlier, all items.
terms.Core CPI: Consumer prices without food and energy, against a year earlier.
terms.PCE: PCE prices against a year earlier: the measure behind the Fed's 2% target.
terms.Core PCE: PCE without food and energy: the Fed's favourite gauge.
terms.Unemployment: Share of people looking for work who have none.
